=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:670-705 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When a check becomes eligible for the 60-second cap during polling, the loop recalculates its deadline as `start + 60`, which may already be in the past and cause an immediate timeout.
  WHY: A check that was recently started when collection began can time out before receiving the intended wait, producing an incomplete and potentially stale snapshot.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:test_check_runs_wait_budgets_and_late_unknown | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The test does not cover a check crossing the 300-second age threshold during polling.
  WHY: The missing scenario does not verify that the wait budget is preserved when eligibility changes mid-poll.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The preceding fresh-merge gate must be merged first."
  expected_change_site: PR sequencing
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: Both the fresh-merge gate change and bounded-wait logic are introduced in the same PR diff; the diff does not show that the gate was merged before this change.
- requirement: "Test the two wait budgets and failure paths"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py — the `test_check_runs_wait_budgets_and_late_unknown` helper.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: All test cases set `started_at = base_time - 600`; no test exercises a check that is recently started on the first poll and becomes eligible only after polling.
- requirement: "Only for the known case, cap the initial context wait at 60 seconds; otherwise retain the current 300-second default"
  expected_change_site: scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py main() wait loop, the `effective_budget`/`deadline` assignment.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The implementation only caps the wait at 60 seconds when the check is already eligible on the first poll; a recently started check that becomes eligible during polling waits the full 300 seconds and then times out.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:main() wait loop, `deadline = start + effective_budget` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When a pending check crosses the 300-second age threshold mid-polling and becomes eligible for the 60-second cap, `effective_budget` drops to 60 and `deadline` is set to `start + 60` which can already lie in the past.
  WHY: A PR whose sole required check started 200 seconds before review kicked in times out after about 100 seconds instead of waiting the full 300.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:test_check_runs_wait_budgets_and_late_unknown | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test does not cover a check that crosses the 300-second age threshold during polling.
  WHY: The deadline regression is not caught by existing tests.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "The preceding fresh-merge gate must be merged first" (the `conclusion is not None` guard in `_build_wait_view`)
  Expected change site: PR sequencing (issue text reads as a sequencing constraint)
  Evidence of absence: Both the fresh-merge gate change and the bounded-wait logic are introduced in the same PR diff. If the issue intended this as a hard prerequisite, the gate change was already on the integration branch before this PR was opened and the requirement is documentary. If it was meant to enforce merge ordering, the two changes should not appear in the same diff.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:main() wait loop, the assignment `deadline = start + effective_budget` (in the 670-705 hunk, just before the `_emit_wait_diag("decision", ...)` call) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When a check crosses the 300-second age threshold during polling, the deadline is recalculated as `start + 60`, which may already be in the past and cause immediate timeout. (2 related items)
  WHY: The deadline is anchored to `start` rather than recalculated relative to the current time when the budget changes.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "Test the two wait budgets and failure paths"
  Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py — the `test_check_runs_wait_budgets_and_late_unknown` helper.
  Evidence of absence: All test cases set `started_at = base_time - 600` (the comment on line ~3404 says "Keep the start age well beyond 300 seconds independent of local time"), so every scenario in `test_check_runs_wait_budgets_and_late_unknown` begins with a check that is already eligible (age > 300) on the first poll. No test exercises the case where the check is recently started (`age < 300`) on the first poll and becomes eligible only after some sleep iterations have elapsed. This is the exact scenario that exposes the deadline-anchor bug in the main wait loop.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "Only for the known case, cap the initial context wait at 60 seconds; otherwise retain the current 300-second default"
  Expected change site: scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py main() wait loop, the `effective_budget`/`deadline` assignment.
  Evidence of absence: The implementation only caps the wait at 60 seconds when the check is *already* eligible on the first poll. For checks that are recently started when the collector begins waiting, the collector waits the full 300 seconds and then times out — the 60-second cap never applies. The implementation matches the literal text but misses the case where eligibility is achieved mid-wait.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:main() wait loop; eligibility is recalculated on each snapshot, then the eligible path sets `deadline = start + effective_budget` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The 60-second cap is applied retroactively from the collector’s original start time when a check becomes eligible during polling.
  WHY: If a required check has been running for 200 seconds at the first snapshot, it is initially classified as recently started; after about 100 seconds of polling it crosses the 300-second threshold, and the deadline becomes 60 seconds after collection began and has already passed.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: “The preceding fresh-merge gate must be merged first.”
  Expected change site: PR sequencing; the fresh-merge gate must be present in the merged base before the bounded-wait change.
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff adds the fresh-merge behavior in `_build_wait_view` alongside the bounded-wait logic; it does not show that the gate was merged before this change.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:main() wait loop, `effective_budget = min(wait_timeout, KNOWN_REQUIRED_WAIT_CAP_SECS) if eligible else wait_timeout` followed by `deadline = start + effective_budget` (around lines 695-700) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The 60-second cap deadline is anchored to `start` and recalculated every poll iteration, so a check that becomes eligible mid-wait can have a deadline already in the past.
  WHY: A required check that was recently started at the beginning of the wait receives a truncated wait and times out prematurely. (2 related items)
